about: The engine's calibration corrections — the same cases in every edition. The engine holds the active calibration (the file 'calibrationFile') and computes its per-bin dB corrections from its own bins: bin i is at i × sampleRate / fftSize Hz, its exact frequency. Each case: the engine at 'sampleRate' (after 'fromSampleRate', when given — the corrections must follow a rate change), with the calibration applied; 'bins' are bin indices and 'expect' the correction at each, within 'tolerance' dB. Expected values are the calibration file interpolated at the exact bin frequency; a correction taken at the whole hertz below (the fault this guards) is 1.06 dB away at bin 15. 'parse' cases read a calibration file's text as the import does: 'file' names a fixture, or 'content' gives the text (lines joined with newlines). 'expect' fields: 'pointCount', 'first' and 'last' ([Hz, dB], after sorting by frequency; within 0.001), 'points' (all of them, when few; within 0.001), 'sensitivity' and 'referenceLevel' (dB, or null when the header gives none), or 'error': true when the text holds no data point. Header lines start with " (UMIK-1) or * (REW); the header names are read as Swift reads them — spelled as written, in any case; a data line is a frequency and a correction separated by tabs, spaces or commas, both numbers in full, kept when the frequency is 1–24000 Hz. 'details' cases: what Settings shows for a calibration read from 'file' or 'content' — 'sensitivity' (null when the header gives none), 'dataPoints' and 'range' (null when it has no points), each the text shown.

cases.note: the corrections are the calibration at each bin's exact frequency (10.99, 11.72, 12.45, 88.62, 1000.49 and 15000 Hz)
after the sample rate changes from 48 kHz to 44.1 kHz, the corrections follow the new bins
outside the file's range the correction is flat: the first point's below 10.054 Hz (bins at 0.73 and 9.52 Hz), the last point's above 20016.816 Hz (bins at 20017.8 and 23999.3 Hz)

parse.note: a UMIK-1 file: its points, sorted, and the Sens Factor; no reference level
a UMIK-1 header's Sens Factor (with a + sign) and SESSION REF
a REW header's SPL is the reference level
tabs, spaces or commas separate; frequencies outside 1–24000 Hz are dropped
header names are read in any case
"Sensitivity Factor" is not "Sens Factor", and a factor with no dB is not read
a number that is not one in full drops the line
points out of order are sorted by frequency
no data point is an error

details.note: a UMIK-1 file: its sensitivity, its points, the frequencies they span
no Sens Factor: no sensitivity line
